decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch both grippers toward a downward picking orientation, keeping each arm in its own workspace; object heights are estimated visually.
Finish downward orientation and hover over the leftmost watch and right-side wooden horse, keeping grippers open.
Descend a short distance onto the centered watch and horse and close; retention still needs visual verification during lift.
Allow closure to settle, then lift vertically to test whether each object is retained before transporting.
Both items appear retained. Carry the watch toward the left half of the middle basket and horse above the right basket, lifting clear of the rims.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller translations and slightly lower carriage height to preserve reach margin while approaching the baskets.
The continuity guard indicates limited overhead reach. Tilt the held items forward and lower the wrists slightly before advancing over the correct baskets.
Release the watch into blue and horse into red, pause for separation, then retreat toward the next objects without crossing arms.
Approach the left chocolate and right silver watch; turn the left jaws across the chocolate's narrow dimension while maintaining downward approach.
Use wrist views for fine centering while descending toward the chocolate and silver watch; keep jaws open until alignment is clearer.
Close on the centered chocolate and watch, pause, and make a short vertical test lift before transport.
The chocolate remained on the table, so reopen and approach lower for its thin profile. Carry the retained silver watch toward blue with a reach-friendly tilt.
Correct chocolate jaw alignment at the contact-limited height and retry closure. Lift and tilt the silver watch clear of the blue rim before further approach.
Bridge toward the last accepted right-arm orientation to satisfy both continuity checks, then lift clear. Retry left closure after a small yaw correction.
Retreat the right gripper from the rim and raise it to resolve contact; the silver watch may have slipped. Settle the left closure and test a small lift.
Adjust the first recovery increment slightly upward to bridge the continuity boundary, then withdraw from the basket contact and verify the left grasp.
Lift the apparently pinched chocolate and start toward white. Open and reposition the right hand downward above the slipped watch beside the remaining horse.
Advance the retained chocolate over white while taking a shallow grasp on the upper silver-watch band, trying to avoid grasping the horse beneath it.
Release chocolate into white and retreat. Lift the silver watch backward clear of the blue rim before any forward transport.
The silver watch is still on the table. Change right jaw direction for a band grasp; approach the remaining black watch with the left arm.
Reduce yaw increments after the guard and continue to low, open-jaw approaches above the two watches.
Make small final centering corrections and close on both watch bands, keeping the right approach shallow above the adjacent toy.
Settle the black-watch closure and lift both watches apart slightly to check retention and disentangle the silver band from the horse.
Carry the retained black watch toward blue. The silver watch has slipped left, so keep the right hand clear and approach the purple chocolate for a later center handoff.
Recover the left wrist away and upward from the rim with a greater forward tilt before transport. Lower the right jaws around the thin purple chocolate.
The black watch slipped at the rim; approach its new tabletop location. Fine-center and close the right hand on the purple chocolate.
Regrasp the flipped black watch. Lift the purple chocolate and bring it to the front-center staging area without crossing the right arm.
Raise the black watch well above the rim before advancing. Lower the purple chocolate at the center staging point, remaining on the right side.
Transport the elevated black watch over blue with ample fingertip clearance. Release the staged chocolate and withdraw the right hand to allow later left-side pickup.
Release the black watch into blue. Approach the silver watch from the left and the remaining horse from the right, restoring downward orientations.
Replan with small increments after the continuity stop. Clear the left rim and center on the silver watch; carefully align the right gripper with the horse at the workspace boundary.
Grasp the now-isolated silver watch with the left hand. The horse moved left, so withdraw the right hand instead of crossing arms or forcing a poor grasp.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating motion: settle the watch grasp, lift backward above the rim, and park the empty right arm aside.
The silver watch is visibly retained. Carry it high over the middle basket with increased tilt for reach and rim clearance; keep the right arm parked.
Release the silver watch into blue, then withdraw to approach the remaining horse from the left. The right hand stays clear for a later center transfer.
Lower the left gripper onto the isolated horse and close, keeping the parked right arm clear and avoiding the basket rim.
Lift the horse backward and stage it near the center for right-side pickup, using a slight lateral tool tilt while keeping the left wrist in its own workspace.
The horse did not remain in the grasp. Reopen and return over its body, aiming farther along the base rather than the narrow head.
The horse shifted into the center-right picking area. Approach it with the right hand while the left hand moves to the yellow wooden toy, maintaining separated paths.
Separate the nearby grippers to remove interference. Withdraw the right hand while slowly centering and lowering the left hand over the yellow toy.
Recenter on the shifted yellow toy before closure and move the right arm farther aside to keep the grasp area clear.
Lift the yellow toy and move it toward a center staging point, with the wrist kept left of center and the right arm parked clear.
Lower and release the yellow toy at the center staging area, a little behind the chocolate so the objects remain separated.
Withdraw the left arm first, then approach the staged yellow toy with the right hand, preserving clearance between the arms.
Fine-center the right jaws over the yellow toy's body and close shallowly, leaving the chocolate underneath undisturbed and the left arm stationary.
Settle then lift the yellow toy outward to the right. Once the center is clear, move the left hand toward the remaining horse's body.
Carry the retained yellow toy high toward red, increasing pitch for clearance. Fine-center the left gripper on the horse's broad body.
Release the yellow toy into red. Reposition the left jaws above the horse's body before another shallow descent, avoiding pushing its base.
Close on the horse's body and test a short lift. The yellow toy appears to have bounced behind red, so move the right hand high toward it for recovery.
The horse is not retained; reopen and center farther over its body for a lower grasp. Descend the angled right gripper behind red toward the bounced yellow toy.
Settle the horse grasp and lift back toward the staging area. Advance the right tool beyond the rear rim and close around the yellow toy.
Lift the recovered yellow toy clear of the rear rim. The horse is now on the right side but not held; move the left hand toward the staged chocolate instead.
Neither grasp is assumed successful. Rotate the left jaws along a joint-friendly path over the chocolate; lower and move the right tool slightly back to center the yellow toy's body.
Complete the left jaw alignment and close on the chocolate. Adjust the right wrist farther behind the rim with a steeper approach before retrying the toy grasp.
Settle both closures and lift to check retention. Move the chocolate away from the center while raising the right gripper clear of the rear rim.
Both objects now appear retained. Carry chocolate over white; lift the yellow toy above the rear rim before pulling it forward over red. Keep both grasps closed until stopped.
Stop before releasing the chocolate into white. Lower and settle the yellow toy over red to reduce bounce, keeping its grasp closed for this chunk.
Release the settled yellow toy into red, pause, then withdraw. Begin resetting the finished left arm while the right arm remains available for the last horse.
Finish returning the left arm to origin. Approach the last horse with the right hand; the yellow toy still appears behind red and will need a more forward final placement.
Use smaller final reset increments after the guard. Center the right jaws over the horse's body, descend to a firmer torso grasp, and close.
Settle the horse grasp, then lift backward and rightward clear of the table and rim. Keep the left arm at origin.
The horse appears retained. Carry it above the front-middle of red with rim clearance, leaving the left arm at origin.
The horse slipped before reaching red. Reopen and approach its new position in front of the basket, returning to a downward grasp orientation.
Carefully center and lower onto the horse in front of red, then close for a fresh grasp without advancing into the rim.
Settle the closure and lift backward without tilting, to clear the red rim and verify whether the horse is securely retained.
The horse appears retained across its body. Carry it slowly over the front-middle of red with only moderate tilt and ample height above the rim.
Lower the retained horse slightly over the front of red, stop fully, and release without a transport motion that could throw it past the basket.
Both horses are now visibly in red. Move above the remaining yellow toy behind the basket, aligning the right gripper for another retrieval.
Lower from the interrupted hover with small forward corrections, which restores reach margin, and close around the yellow toy's body behind red.
Let the yellow-toy grasp settle, then lift vertically clear of the rear rim before moving forward; retention will be checked visually.
The yellow toy remained behind red. Reopen and approach farther beyond the rim and lower around its body rather than closing in front of it.
Back away from the reach limit while lowering the grasp around the toy; the wrist view indicates the last approach went too far behind it. Close only after re-centering.
Use much smaller initial recovery increments after the continuity rejection, then ease back and down toward the toy with the jaws open.
Bring the angled jaws back over the toy's body at the current low height, then close. The wrist view still places the toy too far below the grasp center.
Stop the rim-contacting translation, close at the observed pose, and lift vertically to test the grasp and clear the obstruction before any further transport.
The toy is still on the table. Change jaw direction and use a steeper approach from a clear hover, rather than repeating the rim-blocked grasp.
With the new jaw direction, shift toward the visible toy and descend while moving away from the rim-contacting side; close only after the approach.
Reopen the empty grasp and shift toward the toy's visible center, away from the basket edge, with a small descent before closing again.
The jaws are centered but appear to close above the toy. Reopen and lower gradually at the same horizontal position, which also restores elbow reach margin.
The low approach is blocked by a jaw near the rim. Lift slightly and realign the jaw opening parallel to the rear edge before lowering again.
